title: Stari Grad Travel Guide: Beaches, Parking & Where to Stay
metaDescription: Plan your trip to Stari Grad on Hvar island. Discover the best beaches, where to park, neighbourhood guides, and driving routes from Central Europe.
intro:
Stari Grad appeals to travellers seeking a relaxed, historic base on Hvar island. As one of the oldest towns in Europe, it features a pedestrianised centre with stone streets, traditional restaurants, and a long harbour flanked by pine-shaded pebble beaches. The atmosphere is considerably quieter than Hvar Town, making it well-suited for families, couples, and those focusing on slow travel or exploring the UNESCO-listed Stari Grad Plain.

The prime visiting window runs from May to September. July and August deliver the hottest weather and optimal swimming conditions, though they are also the busiest and most expensive months. June and September offer pleasant temperatures in the low to mid-20s, fewer crowds, and warm sea water, while still ensuring most local businesses remain open.

areas.name: Stari Grad Old Town
areas.parking: Banned inside; use municipal lots outside
areas.beach: 15-20 min walk to Bonj or Lanterna
areas.summary: The atmospheric, car-free centre of the town. It features narrow cobblestone streets, traditional konobas, and ancient sites like Tvrdalj Castle.

areas.name: Priko (Northern Bay)
areas.parking: Street parking and private villa spots available
areas.beach: Immediate access to Bonj and quiet coves
areas.summary: A residential stretch along the northern side of the bay. It offers easy walking access to both the old town and the water.

areas.name: Southern Bay & Borik
areas.summary: A green, peaceful area on the southern edge of the harbour. Visitors stay here for the dense pine forest shade and sunset views over the Adriatic.

areas.name: Rudina & Basina
areas.beach: Short walk to untouched rocky bays
areas.summary: Tiny, rustic hamlets located a few kilometres outside the town. They provide complete tranquillity among olive groves and traditional stone houses.

whenToGo: May marks the beginning of the tourist season, with mild weather and lower prices, though the sea is often too cold for swimming. June brings warmer sea temperatures reaching 22°C, manageable crowds, and fully operational restaurants and ferries. July and August are the peak months; expect sea temperatures around 25°C to 27°C, the highest accommodation prices, and busy beaches. September is a strong shoulder month, retaining warm seas and open facilities but with noticeably smaller crowds and reduced rates. From October to April, Stari Grad enters its off-season; the majority of hotels and restaurants close, sea temperatures drop below 18°C, and the town returns to a quiet, local pace.

faq.question: Is Stari Grad worth visiting?
faq.answer: Stari Grad is worth visiting for its 2,400-year history and relaxed pace. It provides an authentic, quiet alternative to the bustling party scene of Hvar Town.

faq.question: How many days should I stay?
faq.answer: Allow two to three days to explore the town and relax on the local beaches. If you are using it as a base to explore the rest of Hvar island, a stay of five to seven days is ideal.

faq.question: Which is the best beach in Stari Grad?
faq.answer: Lanterna is highly regarded for its natural pine shade and pebble shores. Bonj is the most accessible from the centre, while numerous rocky coves can be reached by a short walk.

faq.question: Do I need a car in Stari Grad?
faq.answer: A car is not necessary for staying within Stari Grad, as the town centre and nearby beaches are walkable. However, renting a car or scooter is recommended if you plan to visit the island's southern beaches or hidden villages.

faq.question: Where should I park?
faq.answer: The old town is a strict pedestrian zone, so visitors must park in designated municipal lots on the outskirts. The main public parking areas are located near the town entrances and the ferry port, requiring a daily fee during summer.

faq.question: Is Stari Grad good for families?
faq.answer: Yes, it is an excellent destination for families. The flat waterfront promenade, calm bay waters, and abundance of natural beach shade make it safe and comfortable for children.
